findings.title: Certificate does not cover wronghost.lab.test
findings.detail: Browsers reject the connection with a name-mismatch error.
findings.fix: Issue a certificate whose Subject Alternative Names include wronghost.lab.test.

findings.title: Loads script from a known-compromised CDN
findings.detail: Sold in 2024 and used to inject malware into more than 100,000 sites (Sansec, June 2024). Whoever controls that host can run any code in your visitors' browsers.

findings.title: Form submits over plain HTTP (password field)
findings.detail: Whatever the user types is sent unencrypted.

findings.title: Active mixed content: 1 script/style/frame URL(s) over HTTP
findings.detail: Browsers block these, which breaks the page; where they are not blocked (older browsers, some WebViews) a network attacker can replace them and take over the page.

findings.title: angularjs 1.5.8 has 20 known vulnerabilities
findings.detail: Angular (deprecated package) Cross-site Scripting; Angular's deprecated package has a Cross-Site Scripting issue; AngularJS Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements vulnerability; AngularJS Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS); AngularJS allows attackers to bypass common image source restrictions; AngularJS improperly sanitizes SVG elements; Cross-Site Scripting via JSONP; DOS in $sanitize

findings.title: End-of-life software advertised: nginx/1.10.3
findings.detail: nginx 1.10.3 is several years out of date. Known vulnerabilities in it will not be patched.

findings.title: No Certificate Transparency proof found
findings.detail: Chrome and Safari require SCTs for publicly trusted certificates. None are embedded, and none came in the TLS extension. They may still arrive in a stapled OCSP response.

findings.title: 2 CDN resource(s) without Subresource Integrity
findings.detail: If the CDN or the package is compromised, the modified file runs on your site. These are fixed, versioned files, so an integrity hash costs nothing.

snippets.html:
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.min.js"
        integrity="sha384-<base64 hash>"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<!-- hash: openssl dgst -sha384 -binary lib.min.js | openssl base64 -A -->

findings.title: MTA-STS policy file cannot be fetched
findings.detail: The DNS record exists but https://mta-sts.lab.test/.well-known/mta-sts.txt failed, so senders ignore the policy. It must be served over HTTPS with a valid certificate.

findings.title: No Content Security Policy
findings.detail: CSP is the main browser-side defence that stops injected scripts (XSS) from running. Without it, any markup-injection bug becomes code execution in your users' sessions.
findings.fix: Start with a nonce-based strict policy, deployed first as Report-Only.

snippets.nginx: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-$request_id' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests" always;
snippets.apache: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; upgrade-insecure-requests"
snippets.caddy: header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'"
snippets.express: app.use(helmet.contentSecurityPolicy({ directives: { defaultSrc: ["'self'"], objectSrc: ["'none'"], baseUri: ["'none'"], frameAncestors: ["'self'"] } }));

findings.title: Page can be embedded by any site (clickjacking)
findings.detail: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors. A malicious page can load this site in an invisible frame and trick users into clicking buttons on it.
findings.fix: Send CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for old browsers).

snippets.nginx:
add_header Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'" always;
add_header X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN always;
snippets.apache:
Header always set X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN
Header always append Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'"

findings.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) not enabled
findings.detail: Without HSTS a network attacker can strip HTTPS (sslstrip) whenever a user follows an http:// link or types the bare domain, and users can click through certificate warnings.
findings.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security with max-age of at least one year.

snippets.apache: Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
snippets.express: app.use(helmet.hsts({ maxAge: 63072000, includeSubDomains: true, preload: true }));
snippets.cloudflare: SSL/TLS -> Edge Certificates -> HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS): enable, max-age 12 months, include subdomains, preload

findings.title: CMS version disclosed: WordPress 4.9.8
findings.detail: The generator tag tells attackers exactly which CMS release (and known bugs) to target.

findings.title: Passive mixed content: 1 media URL(s) over HTTP
findings.detail: Images and media over HTTP can be swapped or used to track users; browsers now auto-upgrade or block them.

findings.title: Software versions disclosed in headers
findings.detail: Exact version banners let attackers match the server against public exploits without probing.

snippets.apache:
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
Header always unset X-Powered-By

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff not set
findings.detail: Browsers may guess ('sniff') content types and run an uploaded file as script or HTML.

findings.title: Extended Master Secret not supported
findings.detail: RFC 7627 binds the session keys to the full handshake and closes the triple-handshake attack.

findings.title: TLS 1.3 not supported
findings.detail: TLS 1.3 is faster (one round trip) and drops every legacy algorithm. All current browsers use it.

snippets.iis:
# PowerShell (reboot required)
New-Item 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.0\Server' -Force |
  New-ItemProperty -Name Enabled -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force
# repeat for 'TLS 1.1', 'SSL 3.0', 'SSL 2.0'

findings.title: 3 third-party script host(s) can run code on this page
findings.detail: Every one of these providers, and anyone who compromises them, has full control over the page. Dynamic analytics/tag scripts cannot use SRI, so keep the list short and use CSP to pin it.

findings.title: No cookies set on the scanned pages
No IPv6 (AAAA) address
findings.detail: IPv6-only clients and networks cannot connect directly.

findings.title: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
findings.detail: COOP severs window references from cross-origin popups, blocking a class of cross-site leaks (XS-Leaks) and tabnabbing.

snippets.nginx:
add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin always;
add_header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-site always;
snippets.apache:
Header always set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin
Header always set Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-site
snippets.caddy:
header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin
header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-site

findings.title: No Permissions-Policy
findings.detail: Restricting powerful features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) limits what injected or third-party code can do.

snippets.nginx: add_header Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()" always;
snippets.apache: Header always set Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()"
snippets.caddy: header Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()"

findings.title: No Referrer-Policy header
findings.detail: Browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, which is reasonable. Setting it explicitly protects users of older browsers.

findings.title: Port 80 (plain HTTP) is closed or unreachable
findings.detail: Visitors who type the bare domain rely on HSTS or the browser's HTTPS-first mode to reach you.

findings.title: No security.txt
findings.detail: RFC 9116 security.txt tells researchers how to report vulnerabilities. Without it, reports often go to the wrong inbox or nowhere.

snippets.file:
# /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116)
Contact: mailto:security@example.com
Expires: 2027-12-31T23:59:59Z
Preferred-Languages: en
Canonical: https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt
Policy: https://example.com/security-policy

findings.title: Key exchange groups: secp256r1
findings.detail: Most preferred: secp256r1.

findings.title: TLS heartbeat extension enabled
findings.detail: Heartbeat is unused by browsers and was the vector for Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). Sitewarden does not send heartbeat requests, so Heartbleed itself is not tested.

findings.evidence: other.lab.test -> Sitewarden Lab Issuing CA -> Sitewarden Lab Root CA

findings.title: DNSSEC signed and validated from the root
findings.detail: Chain of trust validated from the root: . -> test. -> lab.test.

findings.title: SPF record valid (-all hard fail, 1/10 lookups)
Forward secrecy with every cipher suite
No insecure cipher suites (export, NULL, anonymous, RC4, DES, 3DES)

limitations: Passive checks only: Sitewarden sends ordinary TLS handshakes, page requests and DNS queries, the same traffic a browser or mail server produces.
Not tested: Heartbleed, ROBOT, application-level flaws (SQL injection, XSS) and anything behind a login.
